weeks.note: RECOVERY WEEK. Upper/Lower split: two upper sessions (Tue, Fri) so chest and back get 2x frequency at zero cost to running; one lower session (Thu), which is all the race can afford. Only two sessions actually matter: the talk test on a cool morning, and Saturday's descents.

sessions.label: UPPER A (push-emphasis) — bench/press + a row. No leg cost, won't touch tomorrow's test.
TALK TEST 5 km — MORNING, cool, fresh. Step the pace up every 3-5 min, say a sentence aloud, note the HR where it turns from comfortable to 'comfortable but harder'.
LOWER — own day, no running. Strength focus (squat/split squat, single-leg RDL, calf, tib, glute-med). NOT eccentric-emphasised — Saturday is the eccentric day.
Easy run 4 km (talk test) — or the TALK TEST if Wednesday slipped
UPPER B (pull-emphasis) — pull-ups/rows + a press. Second upper session: chest and back both hit 2x this week.
Vertical 25 min (stairs/ramp/incline) — climbing
Controlled stair/ramp descents after the vertical — THE eccentric session. First real descent load.

weeks.note: Barcelona Tue-Fri, then festival at Amsterdamse Bos (Fri evening, Sat, Sun). Down week — the travel timing is ideal; nothing here builds fitness. Benchmark deferred to a cool, recovered morning (Week 6). The long run folds into Sat festival morning. Festival walking covers the volume; do not add load.

sessions.label: Easy 3 km — Barcelona, early AM by feel. Heat inflates HR; ignore pace and HR, run by breath.
Optional vertical — hike Montjuic or Bunkers del Carmel in Barcelona. No benchmark this week; heat and travel would void the data.
Long run 6-7 km — Sat morning from Lelylaan into Amsterdamse Bos, easy by feel; scope the festival grounds. Hydrate hard before the day.

weeks.note: EASY RE-ENTRY — recovering from the festival weekend. No max efforts, no heavy legs, no CP test (moved to Week 6, now a power test on fresh legs). Optional easy 4 km Thu or rest — your call. Run easy by feel, hydrate; only if you feel decent. Getting back to baseline is the whole job this week.

sessions.label: Easy 4-5 km recovery jog — by feel, conversational, ignore pace/HR. Walk it in if you feel rough.
Easy 5-6 km by feel. Optional light pull if you are feeling good.
Easy bike ride instead of the long run — zero impact, aerobic recovery. Keep it chill; save the legs for Tuesday's power test.

weeks.note: First real fitness read of the block — the CP power test, Tuesday on fresh legs (Mon rest before it). Power, not HR: after the sensor audit, power is the channel we trust. This sets your real training zones. HR benchmark is shelved until a chest strap.

weeks.note: RESET WEEK. Two corrections that change everything. (1) You have steep terrain 20-25 MINUTES away - Zuid-Kennemerland dunes by train, faces at 30-45%. I told you the nearest hills were 2.5-3 h; that was wrong. (2) Your plan's vertical is an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE short: 40 min/week is ~400 m against a 2,003 m race. From here everything is measured in time and vertical metres, never kilometres. LOCKED WEEK SHAPE: Sun optional easy ride - MON REST - TUE legs + preconditioning walk ONLY (this is THE eccentric day - keep it focused, no upper) - WED easy run + strides + push - THU vertical + pull - FRI REST - SAT LONG DAY. Eccentric work sits 48 h apart throughout: Tue heavy, Thu moderate, Sat long. That spacing is the constraint - force loss needs 3 days to recover and soreness 4, so 24 h between eccentric sessions compounds damage instead of building tolerance. Cutbacks weeks 10 and 13. CUT ORDER: (1) Sunday ride, (2) Thursday vertical. Never Saturday's long day or Tuesday's legs. HYROX SEEDING STARTS: only via substitution inside Thursday's pull session - erg warm-up, farmers carry, dead hangs. NOT wall balls, sandbag lunges or burpee broad jumps - those are all quad and eccentric load competing directly with the descent block. NOT compromised running - it breaks the 80/20 distribution Madeira needs. The point is to arrive in November with technique and grip already built, so the first two Hyrox weeks are productive instead of remedial.

sessions.label: OPTIONAL easy ride 60-75 min - the day after the long day. Zero impact. THIS IS THE FIRST THING TO CUT when work bites.
Easy run 6 km (talk test) + 6-8 x 20 s strides after (relaxed, full recovery, not a workout)
Push (upper) - after the easy run. Fresh, not on legs you just destroyed.

Legs ONLY, no upper - heavy eccentric. Three quad lifts doing three different jobs: HEAVY BILATERAL trap-bar deadlift 4 x 4-6 at 85 kg (18 Aug: 75x6x3 with 4+ reps in reserve, so 1RM is nearer 100 - autoregulate to 2 REPS IN RESERVE and add 5 kg when the last set still feels easy), LOADED UNILATERAL Bulgarian split squat 3 x 8/leg with dumbbells, and TEMPO ECCENTRIC step-downs 3 x 8-10/leg with 3-4 s lowering. Then Nordics 3 x 5 and single-leg calf raises. Never to failure. 48-72 h before the long day. On a -15% descent hip drop is 23.7 mm vs 7.6 mm uphill (very large effect), so descending is a frontal-plane hip problem and not only a quad problem - loaded Bulgarians carry that demand, which is why standalone side planks and cable abduction came out. HYROX SLED TECHNIQUE at the end, 8-10 x 12.5 m at 50-65% load (~100 kg), 60-90 s rest. TECHNIQUE ONLY, never to fatigue. Forearms hooked on the posts, 30-45 deg lean, short choppy steps 20-30 cm at 3-4 per second, and never let the sled stop. Sled push is PURELY CONCENTRIC, so it costs your descent block nothing - which is why it is the one Hyrox station you can train now. At 56 kg you need 1.03x bodyweight of horizontal force to break a stationary sled versus 0.81x to keep one rolling, so learning not to stop is worth more to you than to anyone heavier. About 8 minutes.

VERTICAL 45 min - STAIRWELL, your own building or a car park. ~12 x 15 floors, about 540 m. Lift up, WALK DOWN - the descent is the point. Dutch stair pitch is 30-33 deg, inside the optimal climbing range, and Madeira is full of stone staircases. Zero travel, weather-proof.

Pull (upper) - after the vertical session. HYROX SEEDING, all substitutions not additions: (1) WARM UP ON THE SKIERG OR ROWER, 5-8 min, technique only - hinge and drive the first third of the pull, that is where 80% of ski power comes from. Replaces your normal warm-up, costs nothing. (2) SWAP one row variation for a HEAVY FARMERS CARRY, 4 x 40-60 m. Same pulling pattern, direct Hyrox transfer. (3) Finish with DEAD HANGS, 3 x max. Baseline 20 Aug was 32/36/31 s, so 90 s by October was never realistic: target 55-60 s by 1 Nov and 90 s by Hyrox in January. Grip takes 4-6 weeks to change and it is what limits the farmers carry. About 3 minutes total added to the session.
LONG DAY 1:50 time-on-feet, 300 m vert. Dunes if you can get there.

PRECONDITIONING DOWNHILL WALK - 5 minutes, 5.6 kg in the pack, walking DOWN stairs. Lift up, walk down, repeat for 5 min. ~110 m of descent, about 37 flights. One bout cuts strength loss 49%, CK 47%, soreness 66% a week later. Five minutes, in your own building, no travel.

weeks.note: Poles introduced this week. They save little metabolically but cut RPE 14-18% and measurably reduce muscle damage over a climb-and-descent day. Length = height x 0.67 = 107 cm, so 105 cm is the correct fit (Mountain King chart: 155-165 cm -> 105 cm). Nobody manufactures 93 cm - 100 cm is the shortest size made. Decathlon only sells 110/120/130, and its own chart puts 155-171 cm on 110, which is also what sub-165 cm coaches actually run. Buy the Kiprun 500 aluminium at 110 cm, EUR 70. Aluminium bends where carbon snaps, which is the right failure mode on wet basalt for a first-time pole user. Ultra X's 2026 race rules contain no restriction on poles.

LONG DAY 2:05, 500 m vert. First session with poles.

NEW SPEED SLOT - easy 5 km with the LAST 1 KM at threshold effort. Comfortably hard, three or four words at a time, HR 172-181 (LTHR measured 181 on the 7 Sep time trial, where 182 was held for 26 min - the old 168-176 band was set before there was a real number). One kilometre, that is all. This is a progression run, not an interval session: you get a real quality stimulus for almost no recovery cost, in a week where vertical also goes 45 to 55 min and the long day goes 1:50 to 2:05. Volume is the thing being added this week - the last km is a taste, not the point.

weeks.note: GUT TRAINING STARTS. Target 60-80 g carb/h by week 14, from 40-50 now, +10 g every two weeks. No drop bags and no crew at Madeira - only ~2 checkpoints, ~10 km apart - so you carry 400-500 g of carbohydrate yourself. Rehearse the weight and the stowage, not just the products. INTENSITY STARTS THIS WEEK, on flat ground: Thursday's vertical stays STEADY because Hyrox is 8 x 1 km flat and stair fitness does not transfer. Target distribution is 80-85% easy, 15-20% hard. ORDER CHANGED 31 Aug - threshold Mon -> Tue, legs Tue -> Wed, easy run + push Wed -> Mon. Reason is measurement, not fatigue: resting HR was 55 against a 50-52 baseline and HRV 78 against an 89 weekly average, which distorts the HR-work relationship in both directions. This is the first structured interval session of the block and its job is to establish what threshold feels like - a reference set on a distorted day gets trained off for weeks. Load is unchanged: three runs, two gym sessions, one vertical, one rest day, Friday still free. Legs on Wednesday keeps 72 h before the long day, the outer edge of the 48-72 h rule. Push stays paired with the easy run, pull with the vertical. STOPPING RULE: the threshold session happens Tuesday regardless of readiness unless sleep is under 6 h or HRV drops below 70.

NO INTERVALS: the hard session moved to Monday on flat ground, because Hyrox is 8 x 1 km on the flat and stair fitness does not transfer to flat running economy. This is now climbing endurance for Madeira - steady, conversational, just keep moving. Dutch stair pitch is 30-33 deg, inside the optimal climbing range.

LONG DAY 2:20, 700 m vert, fuelling 40-50 g/h

KIT REHEARSAL: load the vest to ~2.6 kg with full race carbohydrate (~13 gels plus pre-measured mix) and walk 60 min. Checkpoints are WATER ONLY - you carry every calorie across three ~2h10 legs. Drink mix must stay 6-8%: a 500 ml flask holding 80 g is 16%, and 42% of a 10% drink is still in the stomach an hour later.

PRECONDITIONING DOWNHILL WALK - 5 minutes, 5.6 kg in the pack, walking DOWN stairs. Lift up, walk down, repeat for 5 min. ~110 m of descent, about 37 flights. One bout cuts strength loss 49%, CK 47%, soreness 66% a week later. Five minutes, in your own building, no travel.

THRESHOLD 4 x 4 min, 90 s easy jog between. Warm up 10 min, cool down 10 min. Comfortably hard - three or four words at a time, HR 172-181 (LTHR measured 181 on the 7 Sep time trial - your easy runs sit at 161, so anything under 170 is not a stimulus). Your first structured interval session: threshold before VO2max because it recovers faster and you are two weeks into having a third run at all.

weeks.note: Cutback. Deliberate, and the reason matters: in trail runners, injury weeks were preceded by load DROPPING 16-24% then rebounding 15-37%. Yo-yo loading, not absolute load, is what precedes injury. This dip is planned and the rebound is controlled. RESHUFFLED 6 Sep: time trial held on Monday (Sunday is a full rest day, which is the setup a TT wants - 9.6 h sleep and HRV 98 the night before), pull moved to Tuesday as the recovery day, legs to Wednesday, easy 5 km to Friday, and Thursday's stairwell session replaced by casual football. Three runs held: TT, Friday easy, Saturday long. Push moved Wednesday -> Tuesday: Tuesday is now a single upper day and Wednesday is legs only. Easy run moved Friday -> Tuesday to sit directly after the time trial: hard/easy back to back for the train-low effect, and it moves run #3 out of the post-football Friday slot that has been the one getting skipped. Friday is now empty, which is the better setup for Saturday. Upper moved Tuesday -> Thursday morning: Tuesday is now the easy run alone, and the upper session sits ~12 h before football on legs it does not touch. TIME TRIAL RESULT 7 Sep: 5.01 km in 26:17 timer (31:20 elapsed - two auto-paused stops of 2.2 and 2.9 min), avg HR 182, peak 193, cadence 179. Splits 5:05 / 5:17 / 5:28 / 5:14 / 5:12. Previous best 5 km was 29:15 on 15 Mar, so a 36 s/km improvement. NOT a clean continuous 5 km: 81% of it sat at or above LTHR against 5% in the 1 Sep threshold session, and it opened at 4:09/km for 200 m. Baseline established: 5:15/km sustainable in 8-10 min blocks at HR 181-183, LTHR 181, form holds at 178-184 spm and 100-107 cm stride under duress. SUPERSEDED 8 Sep: retest set for Wednesday 16 September. Stream review showed the first 100 m ran at 3:50-4:00/km and 390 W with LTHR reached at 65 seconds, so 7 Sep measured a pacing error rather than fitness - it is not a retest but the first properly executed attempt. Wednesday, not Monday, so it sits three days clear of the Saturday long day instead of 40 hours. NOT A REAL DOWN WEEK IN PRACTICE: volume is down but intensity is not - a maximal time trial on Monday, an hour of football on Thursday and 500 m of vertical on Saturday is three hard days. Keep Tuesday and Friday genuinely easy, and if the shins are still talking by Thursday, football is the session that gives, not Saturday.

sessions.label: OPTIONAL easy spin 45-60 min - Sunday is now a REST day by default. Take the ride only if you feel good and Monday's run is easy. With a quality session on Monday you need this rest more than you need the ride.

Easy run 35 MIN (talk test) - THE DAY AFTER THE TIME TRIAL, deliberately. This is the one easy run in the week that does more than add volume: you start it with glycogen partially depleted from Monday, and mitochondrial signalling is amplified when a session begins in that state. Do NOT carb-load for it - a light breakfast or fasted is the point. Eat normally the rest of the day and eat properly after Monday's TT; train-low applies to the session, not the day. Keep it genuinely easy, HR under 155, it is not a workout. NO STRIDES - nothing sharp two days after a max effort. Tuesday is this run and nothing else. PRESCRIBED IN MINUTES, not kilometres: at 7:20/km your 5 km was 36 min, and the accepted easy-run band is 30-75 min. Kilometres make the dose shrink as you get faster, which is backwards.

Push (upper) - THURSDAY MORNING with pull as one upper day. Upper work does not touch the legs, so it is free before evening football and free before Saturday. This keeps every day in the week to a single focus: Monday run, Tuesday run, Wednesday legs, Thursday upper plus football, Friday empty, Saturday long.
Legs ONLY, no upper - maintenance. Volume down, load held at 80%+ 1RM.

Pull (upper) - THURSDAY MORNING, paired with push as a single upper day, ~12 h before football. Different muscle groups entirely, so it costs the game nothing and the gym trip is the only one you make that day. Grip work stays - dead hangs 3 x max and a heavy carry - not for Hyrox any more but because grip is a genuine weakness and it costs three minutes.

LONG DAY 2:00, 500 m vert - upgraded from 1:30/400 m. This is the bridge in the vertical ladder: 500 m here keeps week 11's 600 m at +20% rather than a jump off 400 m. It is also over four times your best long-day vertical ever (118 m), so the vertical is the session - the kilometres are incidental. Expect legs 36 h off an hour of football, so start conservatively and let the vertical, not the pace, be the target. Floor is 500 m if Friday feels rough. DESCENT RULE THIS WEEK: WALK every descent. This is a 450% jump on your largest ever descent session (111 m) and the climbing is the point, not the descending. You start running descents in week 12.

5 KM TIME TRIAL - the number this whole plan has been missing. Warm up 10-15 min easy + 4-6 x 20 s strides + 3-4 min rest. Then 5 km flat, hard as you can SUSTAIN. Go out at threshold EFFORT - HR 175-180, pace 5:25-5:35/km. This is triangulated, not guessed: your 1 Sep 4 x 4 min ran 5:27/5:12/5:20/5:23 at HR 175-178, and VDOT off the time trial independently lands on 5:30. Re-anchor after each retest and hold, check in at 2 km, kick from 4 km. Do NOT start at 4:40 - a blown TT gives an unusable number. Flat, no lights, no turns: Vondelpark outer loop or the Amstel. Auto-lap every 1 km. Down week with Sunday rest behind you.

FOOTBALL 21:00 - casual 8-a-side, 1 hour. This REPLACES the 40 min stairwell session; do not do both. The vertical that builds toward Madeira is the long day's, not this one, and cutting it in a down week does not touch the Saturday-to-Saturday ladder. Warm up properly before kick-off - the cutting and decelerating is the highest acute injury risk in your week and an ankle ends the race. Finish 22:00, eat, bed by midnight: Saturday's long day is 36 h later, right through the DOMS peak.

DESCENT LADDER - 6 min walking DOWN stairs with 5.6 kg, lift back up. About 132 m of descent. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SESSION IN THE BLOCK and it is not the long day. Your entire running descent in 14 weeks is 392 m, largest single session 111 m. Madeira is 2,003 m in one day - 18 times your biggest ever. You cannot close that gap in the Netherlands; the highest dunes are 54 m. What you CAN get is the repeated bout effect: one 20 min downhill walk causing minor damage protects for over 4 weeks, and five 8 min bouts protected against a downhill run 5 weeks later - about 42% less soreness and 53% less CK. The dose is small, which is the whole reason this race is survivable from your base. Front-loaded now so protection is banked well before 1 Nov rather than arriving in taper week.

weeks.note: Time trial week. Vertical drops for one week only; six more weeks of it remain. All three strength sessions kept - only the VO2max session goes, replaced by the trial.

sessions.label: OPTIONAL easy spin 45-60 min - Sunday is now a REST day by default. Take the ride only if you feel good and Monday's run is easy. With a quality session on Monday you need this rest more than you need the ride.

5 KM TIME TRIAL - SECOND ATTEMPT. 7 Sep measured a pacing error, not fitness: the first 100 m went at 3:50-4:00/km and 390 W, HR hit LTHR 181 at 65 seconds, and everything decayed from there. THE ONE RULE: the first 400 m does not go under 5:10/km. If the watch shows a 4 in the opening two minutes the race is already gone. Warm up 20 min easy + 4-6 strides finishing AT 5:15/km and NO faster. AUTO-PAUSE OFF. Out-and-back, 2.5 km each way, so wind cancels. Shirt off from the start. Target even 5:15-5:20/km throughout. If the shins burn, SLOW DOWN 10-15 s/km - do not stop. A continuous 27:30 beats a broken 26:17 because paces can be built from it.
Push (upper) - after the easy run. Fresh, not on legs you just destroyed.

Legs - MOVED TO THURSDAY, after the time trial. Heavy eccentric quad work 48 h before a 5 km measures your fitness through muscle damage, which was already baked into 7 Sep. Last legs session was 25 Aug - this one is not optional, and the lower-leg capacity block in it has never actually been done. Legs ONLY, no upper - heavy eccentric. Three quad lifts doing three different jobs: HEAVY BILATERAL trap-bar deadlift 4 x 4-6 at 85 kg (18 Aug: 75x6x3 with 4+ reps in reserve, so 1RM is nearer 100 - autoregulate to 2 REPS IN RESERVE and add 5 kg when the last set still feels easy), LOADED UNILATERAL Bulgarian split squat 3 x 8/leg with dumbbells, and TEMPO ECCENTRIC step-downs 3 x 8-10/leg with 3-4 s lowering. Then Nordics 3 x 5 and single-leg calf raises. Never to failure. 48-72 h before the long day. On a -15% descent hip drop is 23.7 mm vs 7.6 mm uphill (very large effect), so descending is a frontal-plane hip problem and not only a quad problem - loaded Bulgarians carry that demand, which is why standalone side planks and cable abduction came out. LOWER-LEG CAPACITY, about 4 min at the end: tibialis anterior raises 3 x 15-20 (heels on a step, toes lifting), heel walks 2 x 20 m, and eccentric dorsiflexion 3 x 10 slow against a band. The plan had NOTHING for the anterior lower leg and that is the tissue that failed on the 7 Sep time trial - it is also what controls the foot down on every descending step, which is 2,003 m of Madeira. Progress the load week to week. Keep the soleus and calf work as well; this is added capacity, not a substitution.

Pull (upper) - moved to Tuesday. Upper body only, nothing that loads the legs: the time trial is Wednesday and legs stay fresh until it is done. Grip work stays - dead hangs 3 x max and a heavy carry - not for Hyrox any more but because grip is a genuine weakness and it costs three minutes.

LONG DAY 2:30, 600 m vert - trimmed from 2:35/900 m. Your best long-day vertical ever is 118 m, so week 10's 500 m was already a four-fold jump; 600 m here keeps the ladder at 500 -> 600 -> 700 rather than a 50% step onto ground you have never covered - Posbank if possible, descents on hard surface DESCENT CUE: shorten the step, 185-195 spm. Understriding cut strength loss to -8.8% vs -15.5% at preferred step length - roughly halved. Do NOT coach foot strike: the more anterior the strike, the LARGER the quad torque loss. Let the terrain dictate it. WHERE: ZANDVOORT / BLOEMENDAAL DUNES, ~30 min by train. 600 m = about 17 dune reps at 35 m. Sand descent is SOFT - great for volume, poor rehearsal for volcanic rock. Accept that here; the hard-surface work comes at Posbank in week 14.
Easy run 30-40 MIN, HR under 155. TIME TRIAL WEEK - this is a shakeout, not a session. The VO2max block comes back in week 12. Add 4 x 20 s strides at the end, relaxed, full recovery.

DESCENT LADDER - 10 min walking DOWN stairs with 5.6 kg, lift back up. About 220 m of descent. THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SESSION IN THE BLOCK and it is not the long day. You cannot close that gap in the Netherlands; the highest dunes are 54 m. weeks.note: RACE WEEK. Sunday 1 Nov, Calhau de Sao Jorge to Machico. THE START IS 11:00, NOT DAWN - sunset is 18:17 and civil twilight ends 18:41. A 6:30 finish is daylight; 7:00 is dusk; 7:30 is DARK on exposed cliff paths. YOUR HEADTORCH IS SAFETY KIT, NOT A FORMALITY - carry it charged. The late start also gives you an unhurried fuelling morning: eat properly, this is an advantage. CHECKPOINTS ARE WATER ONLY - the 'water and snacks' line is wrong. Carry 420-490 g of carbohydrate yourself (~13 gels plus mix) across three ~2h10 legs, roughly 2.6 kg of vest. Only ~2 checkpoints, ~10 km apart. KIT: 1.5 L hydration capacity, taped-seam hooded waterproof, emergency blanket, 800 kcal reserve, phone with GPX, spare warm layer, and a BEAKER of at least 15 cl - bottles and flasks are explicitly not accepted. Checks are enforced. CALIBRATION from the 2025 field (n=34): winner 3:02:21, median 5:24:37 (13.0 min/km), last finisher 8:03:43, cut-off 11.5 h. Your target is 6:15-6:45. The 25K is the final 25 km of the 50K route - the organiser gave the SHORT race the STEEPEST ground, 80 m/km against 63.5 for the 50K. PACING - the single strongest result in the literature (n=23,207): in 91% of races, slower finishers overspent in the FIRST segment; after the opening everyone paces the rest alike. The damage is done at the start. Hike every gradient above 15% from the gun. HR: race average 138-150, climb ceiling 155, descents 120-140. Above 160 for two minutes on a climb, walk. Your 17 km run averaged 163 - you cannot hold that for six hours. THE DESCENT IS THE RACE. Racing the first steep descent saves ~10 minutes and costs 17-46 minutes later: 3:1 to 5:1 against, before you count the fall risk. And it will never feel hard - VO2 on descents is only 79% of threshold versus 100% uphill, so your breathing will tell you nothing. That is the trap. Short steps, 185-195 spm, gaze 4-5 m ahead on the second upcoming foothold, walk the stone staircases, zig-zag the wet sections. IN-RACE DIAGNOSTIC: compare climb rate per heartbeat on the second climb against the first. More than 5% worse means you overcooked the descent - concede ten minutes immediately and save the day. FUEL: 60-75 g/h at 2:1 glucose:fructose, drink to thirst, skip the salt capsules (no evidence they prevent hyponatraemia or cramp). Carb load 8-10 g/kg for 36-48 h = 450-560 g. Caffeine ~100 mg at 3 h and 75-100 mg at 4.5 h, 150-200 mg total - do not scale from 70 kg examples. WEATHER: use Santana on the north coast, not Funchal - 18 C max, 110 mm of rain across ~40% of days. Wet basalt and hypothermia are the risks here, not heat. Bib pickup Fri 30 Oct or Sat 31 Oct, 18:00-20:00, Machico Forum. No crew, no pacers, no drop bags.
